entwurf.thema: Claude Code with MCP: setup step by step

teile.text: You've become a very tired copy machine. Claude Code with MCP can read your tools directly, so what does that cost? But the bill isn't the only risk.
teile.szene: Painted open-world-game poster style: a black-haired man in a black leather jacket and glowing cyan glasses slumps at a cluttered night desk, hands mid-air as if copying and pasting, neon city window behind, medium shot.

teile.text: The Claude Code MCP page gives a test. Connect a server when you're copying data into chat from another tool, like an issue tracker. By the end, you'll know the claude mcp add command, the plan limits, and when paying makes sense.
teile.szene: Painted open-world poster style: the cyan-glasses presenter in a black leather jacket stands in a neon-lit alley workshop, one hand raised counting on fingers, calm dark upper area, warm rim lighting, medium shot.

teile.name: Install Claude Code
teile.text: First, the install. The overview page says open a terminal and run the command for your system. The install command shows no progress while it downloads. Stare at it anyway. When it finishes, open a new terminal window and run claude dash dash version.
teile.szene: Painted game-poster style: close shot of the presenter's hands typing on a laptop keyboard in a dim apartment, cyan glasses reflecting faint light, the laptop screen turned away from the viewer.

teile.text: A working installation prints a version number. Thrilling, I know. If your shell says claude isn't found, the page points you to Fix your PATH. Then start Claude Code in any project. It prompts you to log in on first use.
teile.szene: Painted open-world style: the presenter leans back in a chair with a small satisfied nod, a coffee mug beside him on a desk, city lights through a rainy window, medium shot.

teile.text: That's the install done. Be sure to like, share and save this video.
teile.szene: Painted poster style: the cyan-glasses presenter in a black leather jacket gives a friendly thumbs up toward the camera on a neon rooftop at dusk, medium shot, open sky above.

teile.name: Add a server
teile.text: MCP stands for Model Context Protocol. Its intro page calls it an open-source standard for connecting AI applications to external systems.
teile.szene: Painted open-world style: a workbench with several different cables and adapters laid out beside a laptop, a hand holding one plug ready, warm lamp light, close-up with calm lower area.

teile.text: Now the command itself. But one of the three options is already deprecated. The page lists three options. Option 1 is Add a remote HTTP server, the recommended option for remote MCP servers. The command is claude mcp add, dash dash transport http, then a name, then the URL.
teile.szene: Painted game-poster style: the presenter types with focus at a desk, three small colored cards laid side by side beside the keyboard, cyan glasses glowing, medium close shot.

teile.text: The page's real example connects Notion with the name notion. That example is the page's, not ours.
teile.szene: Painted open-world style: a tidy desk with a notebook and pen, the presenter's hand writing a single short word in the notebook, soft daylight, close-up.

teile.text: Option 2 is Add a remote SSE server. The page says the SSE transport is deprecated, so use HTTP servers instead, where available.
teile.szene: Painted poster style: a worker in a hard hat carries an old rusty antenna down a ladder from a rooftop at dusk while a newer one stands beside it, wide shot, no text.

teile.text: Some services still expose only an SSE endpoint. Claude Code tries HTTP first and switches to SSE when the server doesn't accept it. That automatic switch requires Claude Code v2.1.265 or later. On an earlier version, pass dash dash transport sse instead.
teile.szene: Painted open-world style: a railway switch lever being pulled by a gloved hand, train tracks splitting into two paths in warm evening light, medium shot, calm sky above.

teile.text: Option 3 is Add a local stdio server. Stdio servers run as local processes on your machine, ideal for direct system access or custom scripts.
teile.szene: Painted game-poster style: the presenter sits beside a humming desktop tower in a garage workshop, hand resting on the case, cyan glasses glowing, warm tool-lit atmosphere, medium shot.

teile.text: Here's the catch. A JSON entry that has a url but no type is a configuration error. Claude Code reads an entry with no type as a stdio server, then skips it. The message tells you to add type http.
teile.szene: Painted poster style: the presenter squints puzzled at an unseen screen off-frame, one eyebrow raised, hand on chin, neon-lit office at night, medium close shot.

teile.text: There's also a shortcut. You can have Claude scaffold a server with the official mcp-server-dev plugin. Claude asks about your use case, then scaffolds a remote HTTP or local stdio server.
teile.szene: Painted open-world style: a craftsperson in an apron sets up a wooden scaffold frame in a workshop while the presenter watches with arms folded, warm light, wide shot.

teile.text: If the plugin install fails, match the message. For Marketplace not found, run slash plugin marketplace add, then retry the install. Recap: the install command, the login prompt, then claude mcp add with a name and a URL.
teile.szene: Painted game-poster style: the presenter counts three fingers in front of a neon-lit stairwell, relaxed grin, cyan glasses glowing, medium shot with calm space above.

teile.name: What to ask it
teile.text: So what do you actually type once a server is connected? The page lists examples under What you can do with MCP. One is Implement features from issue trackers. Its prompt: Add the feature described in JIRA issue ENG-4521 and create a PR on GitHub.
teile.szene: Painted open-world style: a small team gathers around a table of sticky-note-free paper-less planning, one person pointing at a wall map, warm office light, wide shot.

teile.text: Another is Query databases: Find emails of 10 random users who used feature ENG-4521, based on our PostgreSQL database. Analyze monitoring data is next: Check Sentry and Statsig to check the usage of the feature.
teile.szene: Painted poster style: a long aisle of server racks with blinking lights, the presenter walking through in a black leather jacket, cyan glasses glowing, deep perspective shot.

teile.text: A third is Automate workflows: Create Gmail drafts inviting these 10 users to a feedback session. The list even includes React to external events. An MCP server can push messages into your session, like Telegram messages or webhook events.
teile.szene: Painted open-world style: a hand sliding a stack of blank envelopes across a desk while a mail slot glows in a neon-lit street corner background, medium close shot.

teile.text: The MCP intro page adds its own examples. Agents can access your Google Calendar and Notion. Claude Code can generate an entire web app using a Figma design.
teile.szene: Painted game-poster style: a designer sketches layouts on a drafting table with pencils and rulers, the presenter looking over their shoulder, warm studio lighting, medium shot.

teile.text: But the page also carries a warning. Verify you trust each server before connecting it. Servers that fetch external content can expose you to prompt injection risk.
teile.szene: Painted open-world style: the presenter stops at an unmarked metal gate in a rainy alley, hand raised in a cautious halt gesture, cyan glasses glowing, moody low light, medium shot.

teile.text: The page says to browse reviewed connectors in the Anthropic Directory, and add any remote server listed there with claude mcp add.
teile.szene: Painted poster style: a busy night market with tidy labeled-free stalls, the presenter browsing one stall of small gadgets, warm lantern light, wide shot.

teile.text: New terminal and VS Code sessions start in auto mode, where a classifier reviews anything risky before it runs.
teile.szene: Painted open-world style: a security guard in a booth waves a delivery van through a checkpoint after a quick look, neon dusk, medium shot, calm sky above.

teile.text: Best practices has a table of what Claude decides versus what Claude Code enforces. Under What it can touch, deny rules and the sandbox in strict mode are on the enforced side.
teile.szene: Painted game-poster style: a heavy steel gate closing across a street while the presenter stands calmly on the safe side, cyan glasses glowing, dramatic low-angle shot.

teile.text: The page has a rule of thumb. If Claude still misses an emphasized CLAUDE.md line, the line belongs in a hook.
teile.szene: Painted open-world style: the presenter points firmly at a heavy wall switch in a workshop, expression determined, warm tool lighting, medium shot.

teile.name: Other ways in
teile.text: Prefer an editor? The overview page also lists a VS Code extension, a JetBrains plugin, a desktop app and Claude Code on the web.
teile.szene: Painted poster style: four differently shaped doorways in a neon-lit hallway, the presenter standing at the center one, hand on the frame, cyan glasses glowing, wide shot.

teile.text: The web option says no local setup, and it runs on desktop browsers and the Claude app for iOS and Android. Native installations update in the background. Homebrew and WinGet installs don't, so run brew upgrade claude-code or winget upgrade Anthropic.ClaudeCode yourself.
teile.szene: Painted open-world style: a traveler checks a pocket device on a train platform at golden hour while a laptop bag rests beside them, medium shot, calm sky above.

teile.text: Prefer clicking over typing? The Claude Help Center has a desktop route for local MCP servers. Open Settings, then Desktop app, and select Manage next to Extensions. Click Browse extensions to view the directory.
teile.szene: Painted game-poster style: the presenter relaxes at a desk, one hand on a mouse, the other holding a coffee, cyan glasses glowing, cozy evening apartment, medium shot.

teile.text: Pick an Anthropic-reviewed tool. Click Install. Yes, the button is really called Install. Configure required settings, like API keys, in the interface. Then it's available in your conversations.
teile.szene: Painted open-world style: a close shot of a finger pressing a single big physical button on a console panel, neon glow, shallow depth, calm space below.

teile.text: To check connections, click the plus button at the bottom of the chat box, then select Connectors. If tools aren't available, the page says restart Claude Desktop. Then check the extension's settings for missing required fields.
teile.szene: Painted poster style: an electrician in a workshop tests a row of plugged-in connections with a handheld tester, the presenter watching, warm light, medium shot.

teile.text: Desktop extensions support Node.js, Python, and binary MCP servers. Claude Desktop includes a built-in Node.js environment, so Node.js installation isn't required. For sensitive settings, the help page says mark fields as sensitive in manifest.json. Claude Desktop then encrypts those values using the operating system's secure storage.
teile.szene: Painted open-world style: a developer tucks a small sealed pouch into a wall safe in a quiet office, presenter looking on, soft lamp light, medium shot.

teile.name: What it costs
teile.text: Now the Plans & pricing page. Where does any of this cost money? The Free plan lists limited usage every 5 hours and every week, plus chat on web, desktop, and mobile.
teile.szene: Painted game-poster style: the presenter pauses at a shop counter, hand hovering mid-air, cyan glasses glowing, a curious expression, neon storefront, medium shot.

teile.text: It also lists search the web, create files, and run code. But the Claude Code overview says most surfaces require a Claude subscription or Anthropic Console account.
teile.szene: Painted open-world style: the presenter tilts his head with raised eyebrows at an unseen sign, arms crossed, neon alley, medium shot, calm top area.

teile.text: The desktop app section says a paid subscription is required. So confirm Claude Code on your own account first.
teile.szene: Painted poster style: the presenter holds his hand out flat in a stop gesture at a turnstile gate in a transit station, cyan glasses glowing, medium shot.

teile.text: Pro lists more usage than Free, every 5 hours and every week. It's $20 if billed monthly, or $200 billed up front with the annual discount.
teile.szene: Painted open-world style: a customer at a counter taps a hand on the wood, deciding, shopkeeper smiling, warm shop interior, medium shot.

teile.text: Max lists 5x Pro usage every 5 hours and every week. The table's Limit every week row climbs from Limited to 1x, 5x and 10x.
teile.szene: Painted game-poster style: the presenter climbs a wide outdoor staircase of four steps at sunset, each step higher than the last, wide shot, open sky above.

teile.text: The footnote explains the limit. It depends on the model you use, how long your chats are, and how large your files are. The page adds that prices don't include applicable tax, and plans are subject to change at Anthropic's discretion.
teile.szene: Painted open-world style: a mechanic checks a fuel pump gauge at a roadside station at dusk, the presenter's car waiting, warm light, medium shot.

teile.text: Team is for teams of 2 to 150, at $25 per seat if billed monthly. The Team list includes Admin controls for remote and local connectors.
teile.szene: Painted poster style: a small team of five sits at a long table, one person gesturing while others nod, warm office lighting, wide shot, no screens visible.

teile.text: Max also lists $100 a month in API credits to build on the Claude Platform. Team lists up to $500 per month in pooled API credits.
teile.szene: Painted open-world style: a workshop wall of neatly hung tools, a builder reaching for one, golden light, medium shot with calm area below.

teile.text: The Team list adds No model training on your content by default. Enterprise lists seat price plus usage at API rates: US$20 per seat per month, billed annually, with a 20 seat minimum.
teile.szene: Painted game-poster style: a wide open-plan office at night with rows of empty chairs and one person in a leather jacket walking the aisle, cool blue lighting, wide shot.

teile.text: Best practices has a table row called How much it spends. It lists max-turns or max-budget-usd with dash p, and a spend limit you've set.
teile.szene: Painted open-world style: the presenter sets a dial on an old taxi meter in a cab, focused look, neon city reflections on the windshield, medium close shot.

teile.text: Its section Change a default covers sessions that took more time, tokens, or permission prompts than the task was worth. Its opening lines say this. In most cases, your first plain prompt in a fresh session already does the right thing, without setup.
teile.szene: Painted poster style: the presenter turns a single dial from a crowded control board back to its middle position, relieved smile, cyan glasses glowing, workshop light, medium shot.

teile.text: So back to the question. Adding a remote server is one command: claude mcp add.
teile.szene: Painted open-world style: the presenter confidently presses Enter on a keyboard, cyan glasses glowing, close-up on hands, warm desk lamp, calm space above.

teile.text: The Plans page puts numbers on plans and usage limits. So paying makes sense when you reach those limits, or when a team needs admin controls for connectors.
teile.szene: Painted game-poster style: the presenter stands at a fork in a neon-lit street, one path leading to a small shop, the other to a tall office tower, wide shot, dusk sky above.

teile.text: Until then, the page's own test still stands: if you keep copying data into chat, connect a server. Please like, share and save this video for your next setup.
teile.szene: Painted poster style: the cyan-glasses presenter in a black leather jacket leans on a rooftop railing at sunset, relaxed smile toward camera, city skyline behind, medium shot, open sky above.

entwurf.beschreibung: Claude Code with MCP: how to install it, add a server with claude mcp add, and what the official plan limits and prices say. Based on official Anthropic and MCP documentation.
